title: Operation SDK
deliverable: Publish first-party operation scaffolding, descriptor validators, fixture templates and threat-review guidance.
acceptance: A sample operation is added without modifying scheduler, HTTP routes, database schema or handwritten UI forms.
strict_verification: Independent operation author implements descriptor/step/tests/limits without editing transport/UI/domain plumbing; conformance failure catches missing metadata.

title: Operation pack manifests
deliverable: Group operation implementations by capability, version, dependency footprint and platform support.
acceptance: Required dependencies are explicit; removing a pack cannot produce silently incomplete loaded recipes.
strict_verification: Pack manifests bind operation/revision/ABI/dependencies/capabilities/assets/licenses/sizes; malformed/incompatible packs reject before execution.

title: Lazy browser packs
deliverable: Add on-demand loading and an explicit complete offline-pack catalogue.
acceptance: App, engine and pack versions are verified before activation; failed downloads leave a usable previous state.
strict_verification: Large browser packs load only on explicit need/installation, with verified identity and resource budgets; absent/offline packs never upload input. Extend the already-qualified minimal first-party loader/catalogue rather than delaying initial provider isolation to this milestone.

title: Provider replacement tests
deliverable: Run selected operations against alternate providers behind stable semantic descriptors.
acceptance: Replacement requires byte/behavior conformance and security review; provider identity participates where it affects reproducibility.
strict_verification: Swap a real qualified provider and rerun shared independent vectors/error/resource/secret suites; mock compilation alone cannot claim interchangeability.

title: Core-Wasm plugin ABI
deliverable: Specify a narrow versioned ABI for memory, metadata, bounded I/O, errors and capability requests.
acceptance: The ABI contains no host pointers, unrestricted syscalls or implicit network/file access.
strict_verification: Core-Wasm ABI validates handles/lengths/versions/imports/exports; malformed modules, memory growth and host-call amplification fail under limits.

title: Browser plugin sandbox
deliverable: Load plugins in a separate worker/instance with allowlisted imports, resource limits and explicit grants.
acceptance: An infinite loop, memory growth or hostile output can be terminated without accessing app state or persistent secrets.
strict_verification: Untrusted plugins execute in isolated worker/memory with no arbitrary origin JS authority; forbidden imports, network/storage and runaway execution are denied/terminated.

title: Native plugin sandbox
deliverable: Add a reviewed Wasm runtime adapter with fuel/epoch or equivalent limits and constrained host calls.
acceptance: Resource and capability tests cover malicious modules; signatures are not treated as proof of safety.
strict_verification: Native plugin runtime enforces fuel/epoch or process deadlines, memory/table/stack/host-call limits and capability denial with real hostile guests.

title: Plugin package integrity
deliverable: Add manifests, hashes, optional signatures, provenance, revocation and administrator policy.
acceptance: Unknown publishers are not automatically trusted; rollback protection and offline integrity checks have tests.
strict_verification: Tampered/rollback/oversized/incompatible packages reject; trusted identity/integrity never substitutes for sandbox restrictions or safe-code review.

title: Plugin conformance kit
deliverable: Publish ABI vectors, boundary fuzzing, malformed-module tests and example portable operations.
acceptance: Plugin authors can validate behavior without depending on the web framework or database.
strict_verification: Public plugin vectors/malformed ABI/import/memory/work tests run independently in browser/native; example plugins meet the same limits as third-party guests.

title: Component-model evaluation
deliverable: Evaluate a WIT/component adapter using the required JavaScript shims/transpilation where needed.
acceptance: Keep it optional unless browser/native portability and resource enforcement match the established plugin contract.
strict_verification: Actual WIT/component adapter plus generated JS passes browser/native semantics/import/resource/copy tests; optional tooling remains outside the baseline ABI.

title: HTTP server replacement seam
deliverable: Implement a second minimal/mock HTTP adapter and route conformance suite for a future Vef provider.
acceptance: All application endpoints run without importing the original framework outside its adapter package.
strict_verification: Second runnable HTTP adapter serves the same use cases; framing/backpressure/disconnect/origin/error/security suites pass without domain changes. Mocks remain useful unit fixtures but do not close runnable host replacement support.

title: Outbound HTTP replacement seam
deliverable: Centralize identity, user HTTP, object-storage and other outbound clients behind application-owned gateway policy.
acceptance: No native subsystem opens an unreviewed HTTP/TLS path; destination and trust policies survive provider substitution.
strict_verification: All native outbound consumers are inventoried and routed/isolated under owned egress policy; alternate transport preserves DNS/connect/redirect/trust limits.

title: TLS replacement seam
deliverable: Test inbound/outbound TLS and database TLS connectors with alternate/mock providers for future Brynja integration.
acceptance: Trust, hostname verification, ALPN, timeouts and errors remain explicit; browser-owned TLS is documented as outside this seam.
strict_verification: Alternate native and database TLS providers pass real identity/trust/ALPN/mTLS/negotiation negatives; browser TLS is explicitly outside replacement scope.

title: Conditional sibling integrations
deliverable: Add real Vef/Brynja adapter packages only when their APIs and security properties are usable; otherwise ship contract harnesses.
acceptance: The default build works without sibling paths; integration is not claimed complete when only a placeholder exists.
strict_verification: Real Vef/Brynja integration is claimed only against current runnable APIs with target/security evidence; default builds require no sibling directory.

title: Extensibility qualification
deliverable: Demonstrate a new operation, new pack, provider swap and transport replacement through the public contracts.
acceptance: No domain/database/UI rewrite is needed; every accepted extra dependency has a documented purpose and feature budget.
strict_verification: Demonstrate operation/pack/provider/transport additions through public contracts with actual execution and documented dependency/size costs.
